original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Formal F2[Q8] on exactly two arbitrary dirty registers, unit-priced inverse labels x, x^-1, y, y^-1 (24 paid factors = 6 binary rank-one idempotents x 4 labels), free scalar GL_2(F2) mixing normalized by augmentation: exact paid-call minimum for every one of the 64 ordered diagonal pair targets diag([g1],[g2]), including the predecessor's named endpoints diag([z],[z]) and diag([xy],[yx]). Comparison baseline: the complete 64-pair table under the positive label set {x, y} (12 factors).
scope_change_reason: Pair-collision and overlap survey (2026-10-15T04:34Z, complete pagination): the drawn card's neighbouring Q8 objects are claimed or completed in the last hours (discussion 2243 / PR 2248 resolves diag([z],[z],[z]) and the r=3 three-role positive-label minima; discussion 2300 / PR 2303 checks one- and two-factor words for diag(i,j,k) with all-nonidentity labels). The chosen object is open question 1 of the merged predecessor research/q8-central-commutator-pair (PR 1822): 'Does a label set including the inverses compress any pair target?', extended from its two named endpoints to the complete pair family. The predecessor's open question 2 is deliberately not taken because the concurrent PR 2248 covers it under positive labels.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the bit primitive: a complete finite census of one nonabelian register alphabet under a changed pricing rule. No supplier profile, paid reserve, moment or kappa claim is possible (the bit side does not bind); the a < D/E diagnostic does not apply because no candidate improvement is priced.
stop_rule: Complete BFS to depth 3 for both alphabets plus one invertible-factor meet-in-the-middle for bills 5-6; stop once all 128 pair minima are decided exactly. No pivot beyond this family; the r=3 inverse-label triple is recorded as an open question instead.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json (minima, bills, attainment words, layer sizes, ball digests, generator lists) and verify.py (two independent engines, GL_2 conjugation closure, inverse identity, omission and mutated-target controls); written argument in README.md.
author: Aaron Wang
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance (opencode); no independent human review claimed.
